reason: The one-entry panel32 rewrite has the clearest source feasibility evidence and may reduce repeated call and SME transition overhead; the measured sixteen-call version did not show a repeatable gain, so this remains unverified. `cache_blocking` and `n512_fast_path` describe essentially the same rewrite, so they should not consume separate implementation slots. The 64 KiB lifetime change has a plausible footprint benefit but needs broad assembly restructuring. The fused transpose keeps total A load/transpose work about the same and has high mapping risk; its main proposed change is when scratch is written. B-panel packing adds 1 MiB of timed copies, and the prior packed-B result was unpromoted. The three K-loop proposals overlap, while their two-K premise does not match the supplied current full512 loops; verify the source before considering a distinct change. The full-shape transpose proposal requires a generated primitive that is unavailable to this implementation agent. No proposal has measured evidence of meeting 1800 GFLOP/s.
